newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks ease off record run at close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks ease off record run at close.

text.p: The Australian stock market eased off its record breaking run by Wednesday's close as investors booked profits.
Brokers said a large portfolio by brokerage BZW Australia went through the market, boosting trade in a see-saw session.
The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,613.7 points, down 15.2 points from Tuesday's record close and off the fresh intra-day high of 2,635.7 hit earlier in the day.
Volume was active with over A$880 million (US$670 million) worth of trade.
"The market has had a good run and there were a few people that wanted to lock a few profits in," said Gordon Furner, a trader at broker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett in Sydney.

Market heavyweight BHP headed the long list of blue-chip stocks falls. "BHP keeps struggling. When it failed to break through A$19 dollars, some investors started selling off," one Brisbane-based dealer said.
Data released earlier in the day shook off doubts about a housing industry recovery in 1997. A a strong rise in April housing finance approvals helped the building material index to a higher finish.
It was the only major sector to end the day in the positive zone.
Transport and health care group Mayne Nickless was another stock to tumble, down over two percent.
"There is a perception that the Optus float won't happen now until next year ... It is a perception that is not helping Mayne," ABN's Furner said.
Mayne owns about 25 percent of telephone carrier Optus, which has said it plans a share market float later this year.
